messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired for service=inference-hotpath-prod | alert=p99_latency_high | value=1450ms over 5m | threshold=1200ms :rotating_light:
pagerduty: PagerDuty incident #INC-2026 triggered, notifying on-call
maya: Acked. I'll take first responder. @zach @lex can you join? Any quick impact notes?
sara: Support seeing user reports: increased timeouts from embeddings endpoint, a few 504s in last 10m, customers: beta-analytics, internal-staging tests.
zach: Jumping in. Graphs show queue depth on tokenizer workers spiking, tokenization-latency tail looks bad. p95 ~600ms but p99 -> 1.4s.
lex: Noted. We recently rolled hotpath-v2 with updated batching heuristics last deploy ~2h ago. Could be an edge-case with large prompt batches + hotkey routing.
maya: Is there a quick knob? Can we shrink max_batch_size or force single-request mode for hotpath?
lex: Yes. Two options: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 4 (from 16) on hotpath pool, 2) enable circuit-breaker to shed queued requests and send to fallback model (less expensive but lower throughput). Both are runtime flags.
zach: I'll try reducing batch size first. Maya, opening the bridge and marking incident chat as active.
maya: /invite @zach @lex @sara to bridge. Bridge link: https://meet.redwood/incident-3056789999 (joining)
zach: Running command on infra: 
```
curl -XPOST https://ops-api/reload-config -d '{"pool":"hotpath-v2","max_batch_size":4}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
```
lex: Saw the change come through. Watching metrics.
(2m later)
zach: Queue depth dropping slowly. p99 down to ~700ms, p95 stable at ~420ms. Still above target but improving.
maya: Any customer-impact confirmation? Sara?
sara: Support: beta-analytics still reports occasional timeouts but frequency reduced by ~60%. No new 504s in the last minute for internal-staging.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation to level2 (auto) due to sustained p99 > threshold for 7m.
lex: I'm going to flip the circuit-breaker to divert traffic from hotpath-v2 to the fallback pool for requests that match the high-cost routing (hotkey tag). Doing a canary: 10% reroute.
zach: Command: 
```
POST /api/route-control  {"route":"hotkey","canary_pct":10}
```
lex: Canary in place. Observing.
(3m later)
zach: p99 dropped further to ~360ms on canary slice, overall p99 ~520ms. Good signal.
maya: Increase canary to 50% if stable. This reduces risk but we need to watch cost.
lex: Increasing to 50%. 
(1m later)
lex: Overall p99 now 280ms, p95 210ms. Queue depth normalized.
sara: Customer reports now indicate normal responsiveness for affected tenants. No ongoing 504s.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: incident INC-2026 acknowledged by maya and resolved? (manual)
maya: Not yet closing. Will keep on monitoring for full cool-down and then rollback config.
zach: Quick postmortem notes: likely regression in batching heuristic when large prompts + hotkey routing created uneven tokenization distribution, causing tokenizer workers to back up. Remediation path: 1) short-term: reduce max_batch_size + circuit-breaker/reroute to fallback 2) medium: revert batching change + add hotkey-aware size limiter 3) long-term: tokenization sharding and better per-request cost estimation.
lex: Filed issue: INF-4821 with repro and dashboard links. I'll include the exact commit that introduced the batching tweak.
maya: Good. I'll update incident page and notify support + account ops for any post-incident customer outreach. Leaving a watch for 30m.
(30m later)
maya: Monitoring complete. Metrics stable, no further customer complaints. Proceeding to roll back the canary and restore max_batch_size to previous value during low-traffic window with a safety hold.
lex: Rollback plan queued for 02:00 UTC with immediate rollback flag if p99 climbs > 800ms.
maya: Closing incident in 10m unless anything else pops up. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 marked 'resolved' by maya at 3056790450
